title: Marrakech street-food tour by night with a local chef
meetingPoint: Café de France terrace, Jemaa el-Fna – look for the Tourisme flag
description:
Eat your way through the Medina after dark. We start with harira and msemen at the stalls locals queue for, move on to grilled merguez, tanjia slow-cooked in the hammam ashes, and finish with sfenj doughnuts and spiced coffee at a 60-year-old stand.

I'm a chef trained in Fès and born in the Medina; I'll explain every dish, how it's made and the stories behind the families who cook them. Vegetarian route available – tell me when you book.
includes: Written list of every stall we visited
houseRules: Comfortable shoes – we walk about 3 km
Tell us about allergies when booking

title: Sunset camel trek over Erg Chebbi with a Berber dinner under the stars
meetingPoint: Our camp reception at the edge of the dunes (free pick-up from Merzouga village)
description:
Ride into the big dunes of Erg Chebbi an hour before sunset, climb the highest crest for the view, then come back to a candle-lit dinner of tagine and bread baked in the sand. Our musicians play Gnawa drums by the fire and we point out the constellations – there is zero light pollution here.

The trek is suitable for beginners; each camel is led by one of our guides. Private group only – it's just you, your guide and the Sahara.
houseRules: Bring a scarf and a warm layer – nights get cold

title: Golden-hour photo walk through the Blue City
meetingPoint: Outa el Hammam square, by the Kasbah gate
description:
I'm a working travel photographer and Chefchaouen is my hometown. In three hours we walk the quiet lanes most visitors never find, time the light on the famous blue stairways, and I coach you on composition, exposure and editing – phone or camera, any level.

You leave with 20+ edited portraits of you in the best spots, delivered the same evening.
houseRules: Bring your own camera or phone

title: Private surf lesson at Anchor Point with a local pro
meetingPoint: Surf Berbere shop on the main road – boards are waiting for you
description:
Two hours in the water with a coach who grew up surfing these points. Beginners learn to pop up on soft-tops in the whitewater; intermediates work on turns and reading the Anchor Point line-up. We choose the spot each morning based on the swell.

Price is for your private group (up to 4 surfers) – perfect for friends or a family.
includes: Transfer to the best break of the day
houseRules: Must be able to swim 50 m

title: Cook a Fassi feast: market visit + tagine class in a 400-year-old riad
meetingPoint: Bab Boujloud (the Blue Gate) – your host will hold a Tourisme sign
description:
We shop for vegetables, spices and fresh bread in the R'cif market, then cook together in the courtyard kitchen of our family riad: a slow lamb-and-prune tagine, zaalouk, Moroccan salads and almond briouats. Lunch is served on the rooftop with a view over the whole medina.

You'll take home our spice blend and a recipe booklet.

title: High Atlas day hike to Berber villages with lunch in a family home
meetingPoint: Imlil village square (private transfer from Marrakech available on request)
description:
A moderate 12 km loop through walnut groves and the villages of Aremd and Tamatert, with Toubkal towering above. Our mountain guide grew up here – we stop for lunch at his family's house: tagine, fresh bread and tea with mountain herbs.

Around 600 m of elevation gain; anyone comfortable walking for a few hours can do it.
houseRules: Bring 1.5 L of water per person

title: Fado night in Alfama: hidden tascas, petiscos and live singers
meetingPoint: Miradouro de Santa Luzia, under the bougainvillea
description:
Fado is best heard in a room with twelve chairs, not a tourist dinner show. We go to two of the family-run tascas where neighbours still sing, with petiscos and vinho verde between sets, and end on a miradouro with ginjinha and the whole river below.

I'm an architect and lifelong Alfama resident – expect stories about every building we pass.
houseRules: Silence during the singing – it's the rule of the house

title: Argan oil workshop + traditional hammam ritual
meetingPoint: Place Moulay Hassan, by the clock tower
description:
Start with a women's argan cooperative where you crack and grind the nuts yourself and learn why real argan oil costs what it does. Then a private hammam: steam, black-soap scrub with a kessa glove, rhassoul clay mask and a 30-minute argan massage.

Private booking for up to 4 people – couples and small groups welcome.
includes: 50 ml bottle of cold-pressed argan oil

title: Tea ceremony with a tea master and private Zen garden visit
description:
A tea master from a 300-year-old lineage leads a full chaji in a historic tea house, explaining the gestures, the tools and the philosophy of wabi-sabi. Afterwards we visit a sub-temple garden that's closed to the public and sit with the head monk for a short zazen meditation.

Maximum 6 guests so the ceremony keeps its intimacy.

title: Downhill cycling through Ubud rice terraces + water temple blessing
description:
We drive up to Kintamani for breakfast with the volcano view, then roll 25 km downhill (almost no pedalling) through rice paddies, villages and a family compound where you learn how a Balinese house is organised. We finish with a purification blessing at Tirta Empul water temple and a buffet lunch.

E-bikes available on request.
